AND LEARNING POINTS"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EOSCE QUESTION AND ANSWERS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) \u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EWhat is the mechanism of action of insulin at cellular level?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EInsulin acts on a glycoprotein- tyrosine kinase receptors on the cell membrane and it binds to the alpha subunit which leads to phosphorylation of beta subunit.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EThis leads to transport of GLUT RECEPTORS on to the cell membrane which in-turn transports glucose into the target cell( adipocyte and muscle cell);\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EGluconeogenesis is inhibited and glycogenesis is stimulated in the liver cell with the action of insulin on it;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EAll these leads to decrease in the blood sugar hence it usage in hyperglycaemic state;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E2)How do you differentiate a patient clinically on the bedside whether the patient is type1 or type 2 diabetic?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EIn type 1 diabetics the beta cells are 100% destroyed and hence supplemenation with secretagogues(hypoglycaemic drugs) would not benefit the patient clinically whereas in type 2 diabetics almost 10-30% of beta cells are functional hence we can boost them up with secretagogues and increase the production of insulin in the patient making him clinically well( reduction in the blood sugar appropriately according to dose adjustment).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E3) what are the different types of MODY in type 2 diabetics?\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY stands for \"Maturity-onset diabetes of the young\" and was given that name in\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ethe past because it acted more like adult\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Etype of diabetes (Type 2 Diabetes) but was found in young people. MODY limits the\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ebody's ability to produce insulin, but is different than the juvenile type of diabetes\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E(Type 1Diabetes).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere are now at least 14 different known\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY mutations. They include GCK, HNF1A, HNF4A, HNF1B, INS, NEURO1,\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPDX1, PAX4, ABCC8, KCNJ11, KLF11, CEL, BLK, and APPL1.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe key features of MODY are:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Being diagnosed with diabetes under the age of 25.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Having a parent with diabetes, with\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;HNF4A\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGCK\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHNFIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIPFI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHNFIB\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODYI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY2\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY3 MODY4\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODYS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENeonatal hyperinsulinism, early onset, normal renal threshold, macrosomia (common), prolonged neonatal hypoglycemia (20%)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMildly elevated fasting glucose, little glycemic deterioration with age, low prevalence of microvascular complications (retinopathy, proteinuria\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEarly onset, low renal threshold, progressive\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehyperglycemia with age. Microvascular complications may develop over time\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EExtremely rare, presents ni range from impaired glucose tolerance to NIDDM. May impair digestive functions of pancreas\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESevere kidneydisease, pancreatic hypoplasia, female reproducave ordan aonormaldes\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EExtremely rare, early onset ofNIDDM Extremely rare\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMay impair pancreatic digestive functions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eextremely rare\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMya cause neonatal diabetes, antibody-negative DM,I and MODY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eextremely rare\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFrequently causes neonatal diabetes. Rarely causes MODY with mild hyperglycemia\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ediabetes in two or\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Emore\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Egenerations.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Not necessarily needing insulin.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETable 2. Clinical Presentation of Familial Diabetes in Different Gene Mutations\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EType of\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFamilial Clinical\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGene Diabetes Presentation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENEURODI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY6 KLFI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY7 C EL\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY8 PAX4\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY9 INS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODY OI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBLK ABCC8\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMODYII\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EN o M O D Y name assigned\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDMI: type1diabetes melitas; MODY: oynet-stmiurat dioafbthetes:gnuoy NIDDM: non- insulin-dependent diabetes muetils.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESoucre: References 2,,6 7.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProbably
